To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) high levels of childhood sensory processing disorder symptoms are associated with a higher risk of anxiety disorders in adulthood; (b) this relationship is mediated by difficulties with emotion regulation; (c) high symptoms of sensory processing disorder in adulthood may be a consequence of high levels of sensory processing disorder symptoms in childhood, and (d) difficulties with emotion dysregulation may mediate the relationship between high symptoms of sensory disorder in childhood and adulthood and the development of anxiety disorders in adults.
childhood sensory processing disorder symptoms predict an increased risk for anxiety disorders in adulthood, and difficulties with emotion regulation mediate this relationship.
difficulties processing sensory input in childhood may lead, through difficulties regulating emotions, to heightened anxiety in adulthood.

understanding the role of emotion dysregulation in the progression from childhood sensory processing impairments to adult anxiety symptoms and disorders.
how early maladaptive sensory processing might contribute to anxiety disorders.
understanding the relationship among childhood sensory processing disorder, difficulties with emotion dysregulation in adulthood, and anxiety disorders, and how these factors may be interrelated.

childhood sensory processing difficulties may be a precursor to adult anxiety disorders, which may occur in part due to difficulties regulating emotions.
